author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A joint Concord city-school committee has voted to advance a $22.4 million plan for renovating Memorial Field, moving the long-discussed project closer to public review and final decisions by the City Council and School Board.

The Concord Monitor reported that the committee approved the proposal, called “New Option A,” by a 3-1 vote. The plan is about $8.5 million less than an earlier concept and divides the work into two stages.

A first phase estimated at $13.9 million, including contingencies, would rebuild and expand the track, install an artificial-turf field, add roughly 1,000 to 1,500 bleacher seats and address drainage. A second phase, estimated at $8.5 million, would complete additional improvements.

The next steps are expected to include a public hearing, likely in October or November, followed by separate consideration from city and school officials. If financing and approvals line up, the first phase could take about two years. The phased approach gives Concord a way to address the field’s core athletic and infrastructure needs while leaving later work dependent on funding and future votes.
dek: A joint city-school committee backed a two-phase renovation proposal, sending the project toward public hearings and votes by local governing bodies.
headline: Concord panel advances $22.4 million Memorial Field plan
